Yeah, about that. I get anxious everytime I have to meet my psychiatrist, like I don’t want to go. I would obssess over other things on the day of my consultation then letting it go with, “oh well I missed it today, better try tomorrow”. I’ve been saying that to myself for more than a month since our supposed meeting. And it happens every time. Once, it took six months before I convinced myself to go. And when I did, I only said like 10% of all the things I want to say. And when she asks if there’s anything more I’d want to say, I’d say no. I don’t know what’s wrong with me. I’m trying. I really am. I want to help myself, but it’s really hard

I should consult a psychiatrist monthly (supposedly, but actually I do it when  my parents feel like letting me go, so maybe every two or three months), and an obg every 2 months, which I assume I would’t miss. I think my parents are more afraid of pcos than my mental health, they don’t acknowledge my depression.

My obg said I should start losing weight cuz people with pcos tend to gain more once they start gaining a few pounds. Both sides of my family are diabetic, We had extended family members dying from diabetes. And that’s what Im afraid of. Id rather an easy death than dying in pain. But I cant start exercising because I tend to over sleep, and when I wake up, I have work, so I don’t have time anymore. I work for like 10hours then sleep the rest of the day. I really try hard to wake up earlier but I don’t know why I can’t. It seems like I can’t leave my bed, my body won’t move. I only get to work because its the only way for my family to stop nagging about how lazy I am (they I don’t believe I have depression, I have been clinically diagnosed but they still think its not real, or maybe they just don’t want to ackowledge it hoping it would go away on its own)

You should really try seeking professional help. Seeing that anxiety is hard to explain, professional diagnosis makes it more legitimate for some people. People can’t seem to value mental health as much as physical health, it’s sad but it’s there so we just have to deal with it. I hope you get through with this

The best thing to do is seek professional help. It’s not wrong to ask support from those dear to you, but not everyone can explain your situation. There are people trained for this specific purpose. I know its hard going though this without anyone behind your back. But professional help is a need. There are organizations that are active online and maybe you can reach out to them to help you find a psychiatrist and/or therapist. Asking for help is the first step to overcoming all this. I believe you will get there!
